data.name: Intishal
data.long_meaning: The name Intishal is derived from the Arabic root word 'Natha' which means 'to gather'. This name refers to the idea of bringing things together, collecting, and assembling. historical_references.context: Ibn Khaldun refers to Intishal as a fiscal system implemented by the Hafsid rulers of Tunisia to collect taxes from agricultural lands. The system was characterized by the direct involvement of the state in the management of agricultural production and the redistribution of resources among the different social classes.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that The Berber Kingdoms of the Maghreb The name Intishal carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Intishal was a land tenure system used by the Berber kingdoms of the Maghreb, particularly in the region of the Rif mountains. It allowed for a degree of autonomy for local rulers in the management of their territories, while also ensuring that a portion of the agricultural production was collected and redistributed to the central power.
